propositions: A new `commit_and_push_tickets_branch` entrypoint must stage and commit dirty tracker changes under an acquired write lock before delegating to `push_tickets_branch`, preserving uncommitted inbound events and bridge-bot authorship.

The entrypoint must guard against rebase/merge-recovery states by reusing `check_no_rebase_in_progress`: strict mode raises `PushDeliveryError` with `merge-recovery-blocked`, while default mode warns and returns without staging or committing.
Supplied git identity (name/email) must be applied per-command via git config flags without mutating global or repository configuration; ambient identity is used when omitted.

Lock, staging, and commit failures must raise the dependency-defined `PushDeliveryError` with stable reasons (`commit-lock-timeout`, `stage-failed`, `commit-failed`) in strict mode and warn-and-return without push in default mode, retaining uncommitted content for retry.

A clean but locally-ahead tracker must push without creating an empty commit; persistent rejection under strict mode must preserve the local commit and raise `PushDeliveryError` rather than return success.

The direct `push_tickets_branch` primitive remains push-only and must never stage or commit a dirty tree; the new `commit-and-push` CLI action must co-exist with the unchanged `push` action in the module CLI boundary.
